objective: FU-23 / TR-D-3: ids of rescue_requests, planning_runs, plan_versions and images are never reused after a hard delete, and model_spend.request_id is a foreign key; SEC-R-1: the general per-user limit fails open for GET and HEAD on a busy write lock and stays fail-closed for everything else.
context: Phase D review rev-mv33xoyz-0143dd56 (TR-D-3), security draft phase-d-security-1.md section F (probe ev:ev-mv33e5qp-017ba56b, decision dec-mv330std-0165d9be) and rework-1 review rework-1-1.json (SEC-R-1). Migration 006 is app-only. The runner (src/db/migrate.js) applies a file inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE with foreign_keys = ON, which cannot be switched off inside a transaction, so the rebuild uses defer_foreign_keys = ON and TEMP staging tables. DROP TABLE runs an implicit DELETE that fires ON DELETE CASCADE, so extractions, requirements, replan_queue and plan_approvals are staged and put back with their ids; non-cascading children (reservations, supplier_orders, payment_operations, provider_calls) stay and are satisfied again when the parent ids are re-inserted; a parent that does not come back fails the COMMIT on the deferred foreign key and rolls everything back. Tables are recreated under their own names, so no RENAME rewrites other tables. The SEC-B-2 triggers sit on audit_events and inventory_ledger, which are not touched. CHOICE for model_spend.request_id: FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES rescue_requests(id) ON DELETE SET NULL. The row is the budget ledger (gate.js sums every row of the day), so it must survive a hard delete of its request, and SET NULL drops only the pointer so it can never name another request; an insert naming a request that does not exist is refused. A CHECK cannot look at another table, and a tombstone reference would add a second source of truth to keep. Rows that already point at a deleted request are copied with NULL. SEC-R-1: take(userId, { method, log, requestId }) in src/auth/general-limit.js; GET/HEAD busy error -> return uncounted plus one warn line rate_limit.busy_open (requestId only), reads wait readBusyWaitMs (default 50 ms) instead of the connection busy timeout and the timeout is restored; other methods and a call with no method rethrow the busy error unchanged (the app maps it to 503 DB_BUSY); 429 over the limit is unchanged.
